title: Couture, Crystals and a Whole Lot of Attitude: Inside Bollywood Hungama's Style Icons Summit 2026
excerpt: Vaani Kapoor, Nawazuddin Siddiqui, Pooja Hegde and a small army of OTT's most-watched faces turned a Mumbai daylong fashion summit into the year's most opinionated red carpet.
body:
It started before noon and ran until the lights dimmed past ten — and somewhere in those twelve hours, Mumbai's most photographed people stopped pretending fashion is frivolous. The Bollywood Hungama Style Icons Summit and Awards 2026 rolled out across June 24, and it did the thing the Indian style calendar rarely manages: it put the clothes and the conversation on the same stage.

The arrivals alone were a mood. Vaani Kapoor swept in looking every inch the cover star she keeps threatening to become, all clean lines and quiet confidence. Mithila Palkar — the girl-next-door who became a streaming-era icon — brought her signature unfussy charm. Ahsaas Channa, fresh off her Cannes turn for Gudgudi, proved the festival glow hadn't faded. And then there was Nawazuddin Siddiqui, who has somehow turned not caring about fashion into the most magnetic look in the room. The man wears tailoring like a dare, and you cannot stop watching.

What sets the BH Style Icons format apart from the usual flashbulb-and-flee red carpet is that nobody got to just pose and leave. The day was built around panels — seven of them — each stacked with names that would headline a film festival on their own.

The morning opened with Rohit Saraf, Aparshakti Khurana, Shehnaaz Gill and Sayani Gupta dissecting the tyranny and gift of Instagram-era style. By midday, Pooja Hegde, Gauahar Khan, Wamiqa Gabbi, Kirti Kulhari and Prajakta Koli were arguing whether style and fashion are the same coin or different beasts entirely. Tamannaah Bhatia — who's been refreshingly blunt lately about the male gaze in South cinema — joined Aditi Rao Hydari, Kriti Kharbanda, Karishma Tanna and others to debate whether showbiz and style are old partners or just using each other.

The most candid session may have been the one on pap culture. Mouni Roy, Rakul Preet Singh, Nora Fatehi, Fatima Sana Shaikh and Shriya Saran sat down to talk about a question every Indian celebrity now lives with: does the relentless airport-paparazzi machine put unbearable pressure on how you look the moment you step out your front door? Anyone who's seen a star photographed buying groceries in full glam knows the stakes are real.

Style and showbiz: age-old partners, or mutual beneficiaries? — a panel title that doubled as the summit's thesis

And then there was the closer that made the cinephiles lean in: the Heera Mandi session, a tribute to classic, timeless glamour featuring Manisha Koirala, Richa Chadha, Aditi Rao Hydari and Fardeen Khan. Sanjay Leela Bhansali's opulent world has become shorthand for a certain kind of maximalist Indian beauty, and watching its stars hold court on legacy and elegance felt like the right note to end on.

The awards themselves rewarded a refreshingly wide field — not just the A-listers, but the OTT generation that's quietly become the country's most-watched. Bhumi Pednekar, Sanya Malhotra, Shobhita Dhulipala, Rasika Dugal and Gulshan Devaiah were among the faces moving between the panel chairs and the trophy table, a reminder that in 2026, the line between film star and streaming star has all but dissolved.

For the diaspora watching from afar, the BH Style Icons content is the gift that keeps giving — Bollywood Hungama rolls out the panels and red-carpet galleries on its YouTube and social channels through the week, no subscription required, so the looks and the unusually frank conversations land in the US, UK and Canada the same day they happen in Mumbai. It's become an annual ritual for the fashion-obsessed desi abroad: equal parts eye candy and industry gossip, served with the kind of opinions Indian celebrities rarely offer on the record.

Here's the quiet takeaway from a day this long: Indian fashion has finally stopped apologising for taking itself seriously. The crystals and couture were dazzling, sure. But the real flex of Style Icons 2026 was the willingness to sit down, mic up, and actually argue about what any of it means.
